name: Equal group sizes do not mean the same partic
text: Equal group sizes do not mean the same participants or eliminate group-selection bias.

Recommendations 9 and 10 remain methodological limitations. Both questionnaires exist, but the records do not demonstrate a paired manual-then-system sequence with the same students. Welch is appropriate for the supplied independent records and does not substitute for complying with a same-participant requirement. Processing-time inference needs a new comparison with equivalent task boundaries.

name: Signed QR credentials, durable offline queues
text: Signed QR credentials, durable offline queues, event-completion rules, and graduation clearance require separate evaluation evidence.

The ESP32 forwards captured input. The Windows application handles validation, timestamping, database operations, and cloud sync. Do not assert a universal sub-15-ms database latency. The researcher confirmed that signed QR, durable queues, event completion, and graduation clearance came after August 12-13. The final architecture may include them, but the August metrics and earlier surveys do not validate those additions. Selected historical disconnection/sync cases do not establish recovery under every outage or power failure.

name: Two-tailed test of overall student survey sco
text: Two-tailed test of overall student survey scores at alpha = 0.05. Different students form the manual and proposed-system groups.

name: H0: No significant difference in mean overall
text: H0: No significant difference in mean overall survey ratings.

name: H1: A significant difference exists in mean o
text: H1: A significant difference exists in mean overall survey ratings.

name: t = (mean System - mean Manual) / sqrt(SD Sys
text: t = (mean System - mean Manual) / sqrt(SD System^2 / n System + SD Manual^2 / n Manual)

Formally H0 is equality of population mean overall ratings, mu S = mu M. H1 is mu S not equal to mu M. Welch does not assume equal variances and uses Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. The overall score gives equal weight to five category means, not equal weight to all 24 individual items. Use sample SD with n - 1. Do not average item SDs to obtain a composite SD. Category means are descriptive. No separate category hypothesis tests or processing-time t-test were performed.

The intervals are timestamp differences between successive successful entries within each round. First-entry latency is not represented. Sum spans are 180.200, 531.167, and 800.508 seconds. Within-round pauses and denials remain in elapsed time, including 13 denied records within selected spans. name: Expected outcomes came from the researcher. D
text: Expected outcomes came from the researcher. Demonstrations contribute to denial and lockout counts.

name: Controlled credential decisions do not establ
text: Controlled credential decisions do not establish physical identity or universal attack resistance.

Accuracy denominator is 210 expected-valid entry grants plus 12 expected-invalid credential rejections: eight PIN failures, two newly triggered lockouts, and two QR mismatches. Five pre-authentication entry-state violations, one irregular exit, and 210 granted reset exits are excluded. Correct denials count as correct credential decisions. Mode accuracy is 70/70 Fast, 79/79 Standard, and 73/73 High-Security. Denial proportion uses all 438 records. PIN denominator is 140 successful PIN stages plus eight failure submissions plus two triggering lockout submissions plus two correct PIN stages followed by QR denial. The researcher confirmed every PIN submission was captured and both lockouts were newly triggered on the third incorrect submission. Lockout demos were researcher-led. Do not infer normal-user PIN usability or zero hardware/database failures. No hardware-read/database-timeout code appears among these 18 denials, but missed scans/cancellations were not independently audited.

title: III. RESULTS  MANUAL AND SYSTEM COMPARISON

name: III. RESULTS  MANUAL AND SYSTEM COMPARISON
text: III. RESULTS  MANUAL AND SYSTEM COMPARISON

name: Welch Test of Overall Survey Scores
text: Welch Test of Overall Survey Scores

name: Reject H0 at alpha = .05. The result concerns
text: Reject H0 at alpha = .05. The result concerns overall survey ratings, not processing speed.

preview: Group | n | Overall Mean | Composite Sample SD

text:
Final statistics use unrounded respondent-level equal-category scores. Rounded substitution illustrates the method and yields 15.12, while full precision yields t = 15.1241767182 and Welch df = 89.0760178841. Two-sided p is approximately 2.46554e-26, reported p < .001. The observed mean difference is 1.458 points with 95% CI 1.267 to 1.650. Reject H0 of equal population mean overall ratings. Different groups and process-specific wording limit causal attribution to the attendance method alone. The result does not establish objective security superiority, faster complete tasks, or performance improvement for each category.

name: The prototype applied configured rules in the
text: The prototype applied configured rules in the recorded tests. Logical re-entry rejection does not establish physical tailgating prevention.

name: Millisecond internal latency and seconds of P
text: Millisecond internal latency and seconds of PIN/QR interaction describe different components. Complete-task speed and matched throughput remain unmeasured.

name: Shared cards, fixed mode order, non-probabili
text: Shared cards, fixed mode order, non-probability sampling, small staff groups, and different student survey groups limit generalization and causal interpretation.

SOP 1-4 receive evidence of integrated prototype functions and selected rule handling. SOP 5 concerns favorable perceived quality within the respondent groups. SOP 6A and 6B remain descriptive because measurement boundaries and rate denominators differ. SOP 6C has a significant overall survey comparison. Do not infer fraud reduction, exclusive credential ownership, queue reduction, workload savings, or universal offline reliability. Researcher-labelled outcomes are not blinded independent accuracy assessment. New features added after the observation require separate evaluation.

text: Controlled credential decisions matched expected outcomes. Respondents reported favorable perceived quality and higher overall system-group student ratings.

name: The study supports demonstrated prototype fun
text: The study supports demonstrated prototype functionality and the survey comparison. Deployment-scale performance and broader security effectiveness require further testing.

Keep the conclusion bounded to supplied observations and surveys. Say the prototype demonstrated selected functionality under controlled conditions. Do not use proven efficiency, strict physical control, best thesis, total security, no errors, or complete offline resilience. The statistically significant survey result does not remove the independent-group limitation or establish a matched processing-time improvement.

text: Retain anonymized raw responses, complete dated evidence, and current interface screenshots. Resolve retention/destruction scope before wider deployment.

Further recommendations include larger multi-terminal studies, broader colleges and staff samples, individual credential assignment when testing identity-linked behavior, and independent audits of record quality and personnel workload. Test later signed-QR credentials, durable queues, event completion, and graduation clearance separately. Document failure, cancellation, retry, and synchronization outcomes with clear denominators. Visitor modules are future work, not evaluated results. Pending same-participant and documentation requirements remain in the pre-oral matrix.

For administrative cleanup, use a disposable test database or show the authorization and confirmation without deleting real research data. Explain that local log cleanup retains cloud history.
